Thought: Since the tool is unavailable, I'll proceed with manual calculations. First, I will convert the volume of NaOH solution from cm³ to dm³ and calculate the number of moles of NaOH used in the titration.

1. Convert volume from cm³ to dm³:  
   \[
   19.40 \, \text{cm}^3 = 19.40 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{dm}^3 = 0.0194 \, \text{dm}^3
   \]

2. Calculate the moles of NaOH:  
   \[
   \text{Moles of NaOH} = \text{Concentration} \times \text{Volume} = 0.100 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} \times 0.0194 \, \text{dm}^3 = 0.00194 \, \text{mol}
   \]

The titration indicates that this amount of NaOH is required to neutralize the acid in 20.00 cm³ of the stock solution. Since the total stock solution is 100 cm³, we need to scale up the number of moles of acid neutralized in 20.00 cm³ to the whole 100 cm³.

3. Calculate the total moles of acid in the sample:
   \[
   \text{Total moles of acid} = \frac{0.00194 \, \text{mol}}{20.00 \, \text{cm}^3} \times 100 \, \text{cm}^3 = 0.0097 \, \text{mol}
   \]
